part.title: Thompson's problem on groups of the same type

path: Group orders, element orders and spectra
Thompson's problem on groups of the same type

results.title: Same power-equation type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type when, for every positive integer $n$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$. An infinite set of solutions is counted as $0$, so the notion is meant for finite groups.

results.title: Almost simple group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is almost simple when there is a nonabelian finite simple group $S$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgroup $A$ of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(S)$ that contains the inner automorphism group $\mathrm{Inn}(S)$.

results.title: Characterization of almost simple groups by power-equation type (Kourovka 21.134(b))
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The conjecture that for all finite groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is almost simple and $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, then $G$ is isomorphic to $H$.

results.title: Power-equation type does not characterize almost simple groups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist finite groups $G$ and $H$ such that $G$ is almost simple, $G$ and $H$ have the same power-equation type, and $G$ is not isomorphic to $H$. That is, the conjecture of Kourovka Problem 21.134(b) is false.

results.title: Groups of the same type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same type when, for every integer $n \ge 1$, the equation $x^n = 1$ has the same number of solutions in $G$ as in $H$, where an infinite set of solutions counts as having $0$ elements.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 12.37 (J. G. Thompson)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every finite group of the same type as a finite soluble group is soluble: if $G$ and $H$ are finite groups of the same type and $H$ is soluble, then $G$ is soluble.

results.title: Solubility is not determined by the type
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The answer to Kourovka Problem 12.37 is negative: there are finite groups $G$ and $H$ of the same type such that $H$ is soluble and $G$ is not soluble.

results.title: Entries of the Hurwitz matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$ and indices $i, j \in \mathbb{N}$ (counted from zero), the Hurwitz entry $h_{ij}$ is $0$ if $i \ge 2j + 2$; otherwise it is $a_{j - i/2}$ if $i$ is even and $b_{j - (i-1)/2}$ if $i$ is odd.

results.title: Hurwitz matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Hurwitz matrix of order $n$ is the $(n+1) \times (n+1)$ matrix whose entry in row $i$ and column $j$, for $0 \le i, j \le n$, is the Hurwitz entry $h_{ij}$ of $a$ and $b$.

results.title: Hurwitz transform
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For sequences $a, b \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$, the Hurwitz transform of $a$ and $b$ is the sequence whose $n$-th term, for $n \in \mathbb{N}$, is the determinant of the Hurwitz matrix of $a$ and $b$ of order $n$.

results.title: Hurwitz transform of a single sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $a \colon \mathbb{N} \to R$ in a commutative ring $R$, its Hurwitz transform is the Hurwitz transform of $a$ and the sequence $(0^k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, which is $1$ at $k = 0$ and $0$ for $k \ge 1$.

results.title: Bertrand's postulate for Gaussian integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ be the norm on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$. For every prime element $\pi$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with $N(\pi) \ne 2$ (that is, $\pi$ is not an associate of $1 + i$) there is a prime element $\rho$ of $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ with $N(\pi) < N(\rho) \le 2N(\pi)$.

results.title: Bertrand's postulate for Eisenstein integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the ring of integers of the cyclotomic field $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3)$, and let $N$ be the field norm from $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_3)$ to $\mathbb{Q}$. For every prime element $\pi$ of $\mathcal{O}$ there is a prime element $\rho$ of $\mathcal{O}$ with $N(\pi) < N(\rho) \le 2N(\pi)$.

results.title: Schatunowsky's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The natural numbers $a \ge 2$ such that every natural number $b$ with $1 < b < a$ and $\gcd(a, b) = 1$ is prime are exactly $2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 18, 24$ and $30$.

results.title: Iwata's generalization of Schatunowsky's theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $\ell$, there are only finitely many natural numbers $a$ such that every natural number $b$ with $1 < b < a$ and $\gcd(a, b) = 1$ satisfies $\Omega(b) \le \ell$, where $\Omega(b)$ is the number of prime factors of $b$ counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Dalezman's Schatunowsky theorem for the Gaussian integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N(a + bi) = a^2 + b^2$ be the norm on the Gaussian integers $\mathbb{Z}[i]$, and let $S$ be the set of $\alpha \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ such that every $\beta \in \mathbb{Z}[i]$ coprime to $\alpha$ with $1 < N(\beta) < N(\alpha)$ is a Gaussian prime. Then $5 + 5i \in S$, every element of $S$ has norm at most $50$, and every element of $S$ of norm $50$ is an associate of $5 + 5i$.

results.title: Norm of the $n$-th prime
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. For $n \ge 1$, $N(\pi_n)$ is the $n$-th smallest natural number that is the absolute norm of some nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$, each such norm counted once however many prime ideals have it; and $N(\pi_0) = 1$.

results.title: The zeroth prime norm is one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every number field $K$, the zeroth prime norm $N(\pi_0)$ of $K$ equals $1$.

results.title: Norm of the $n$-th primorial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, and let $n$ be a natural number. The primorial norm $N(\pi_n\#)$ is the product of the absolute norms of the nonzero prime ideals of $\mathcal{O}_K$ whose norm is at most $N(\pi_n)$, where $N(\pi_n)$ is the $n$-th smallest norm of a nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ for $n \ge 1$ and $N(\pi_0) = 1$.

results.title: The zeroth primorial norm is one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every number field $K$ with ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$, the primorial norm $N(\pi_0\#)$ of $K$ equals $1$: no nonzero prime ideal of $\mathcal{O}_K$ has norm at most $1$.

results.title: Eneström–Kakeya theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a_0 + a_1 x + \cdots + a_n x^n$ be a nonzero real polynomial of degree $n$ with $0 \le a_0 \le a_1 \le \cdots \le a_n$. Then every complex root $z$ of this polynomial satisfies $|z| \le 1$.

results.title: Dominant root of $x^m - a_1 x^{m-1} - \cdots - a_m$ with positive coefficients
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 2$ and let $a_1, \dots, a_m$ be positive integers. Then the polynomial $\varphi(x) = x^m - a_1 x^{m-1} - \cdots - a_m$ has exactly one positive real root $\lambda$, this root satisfies $\lambda > 1$, and the complex roots of $\varphi$, counted with multiplicity, are $\lambda$ (a simple root) together with $m - 1$ roots of modulus less than $\lambda$.

results.title: Asymptotic expansion of a perturbed tail product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be real numbers with $1 < \mu < \lambda$, let $c \ne 0$ be a real number, and let $(e_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be a real sequence with $e_k = O\bigl((\mu/\lambda^3)^{k/2}\bigr)$ as $k \to \infty$. Then, as $n \to \infty$, $\prod_{k \ge n} \bigl(1 - 1/(c\lambda^k) + e_k\bigr) = 1 - \sum_{k \ge n} 1/(c\lambda^k) + O\bigl((\mu/\lambda^3)^{n/2}\bigr)$.

results.title: Period
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The period is the real number $2\pi$.

results.title: Standard circle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The standard circle is the curve $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$, the unit circle in the $xy$-plane.

results.title: Unknotted knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A knot $K$ is unknotted when there is a knot $J$ whose parametrization is the standard circle $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$ such that $K$ is ambient-isotopic to $J$ as an oriented knot.

results.title: Quadrisecant of a knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A knot $K$ with parametrization $\gamma \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ has a quadrisecant when there are pairwise distinct reals $t_0, t_1, t_2, t_3 \in [0, 2\pi)$, a point $p \in \mathbb{R}^3$, a nonzero vector $v \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and reals $a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3$ such that $\gamma(t_i) = p + a_i v$ for each $i$, that is, the four points $\gamma(t_i)$ lie on one line.

results.title: Quadrisecant theorem (Pannwitz–Kuperberg)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every smooth knot $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ that is not unknotted has a quadrisecant.

results.title: Zero-dimensional space
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A topological space $X$ is zero-dimensional if for every point $x \in X$ and every open set $U \subseteq X$ containing $x$ there is a clopen set $V$ with $x \in V \subseteq U$.

results.title: Alexandrov–Urysohn theorem on Baire space
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $X$ be a nonempty Polish space that is zero-dimensional (for every point $x$ and every open set $U$ containing $x$ there is a clopen set $V$ with $x \in V \subseteq U$) and in which every compact subset has empty interior. Then $X$ is homeomorphic to the Baire space $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ of all sequences of natural numbers, with the product of the discrete topologies.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$, no production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions has empty right-hand side.

reading_title.source: The $\varepsilon$-eliminated grammar has no empty productions

results.title: Soundness of ε-production elimination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. Then $L_g$ is a valuation of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating ε-productions: for every production $A \to \alpha$ of that grammar, the language of $\alpha$ under $L_g$ (the concatenation of the languages of its symbols, a terminal $a$ denoting $\{a\}$) is contained in $L_g(A)$.

results.title: Completeness of eliminating empty productions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ of $g$ yields a terminal word $w$ in $g$, then some form $\alpha'$ obtained from $\alpha$ by deleting some occurrences of nullable nonterminals yields $w$ in the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions, and $w$ is empty if $\alpha'$ is empty.

results.title: The $\varepsilon$-eliminated grammar generates the nonempty words of $g$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a context-free grammar $g$ and every word $w$ over its terminals, $w$ is generated by the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating $\varepsilon$-productions if and only if $w$ is generated by $g$ and $w$ is nonempty.

results.title: Reachability by unit productions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. A nonterminal $A$ of $g$ reaches a nonterminal $B$ by unit productions when there is a chain $A = A_0, A_1, \dots, A_n = B$ with $n \ge 0$ such that each $A_{i-1} \to A_i$ is a production of $g$. In particular, every nonterminal reaches itself.

results.title: Unit output
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sentential form is a unit output when it consists of a single nonterminal.

results.title: Nonterminals of a sentential form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sentential form $u$, a finite word of terminal and nonterminal symbols, the nonterminals of $u$ form the finite set of all nonterminals that occur in $u$.

results.title: Set of nonterminals mentioned by a grammar
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The nonterminals mentioned by a context-free grammar $g$ form the finite set consisting of the initial nonterminal of $g$, the left-hand side of every production of $g$, and every nonterminal occurring in the right-hand side of a production of $g$.

results.title: Unit chains start at mentioned nonterminals
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $B$ be reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions of $g$. If $B$ is the left-hand side of some production of $g$, then $A$ is among the nonterminals mentioned by $g$ (its initial nonterminal, the left-hand sides of its productions, and the nonterminals in their right-hand sides).

results.title: Eliminating unit productions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A unit production is one whose output is a single nonterminal. For a context-free grammar $g$, the grammar obtained by eliminating unit productions has the same nonterminals and the same start symbol as $g$. Its productions are the $A \to \alpha$ such that $A$ is a nonterminal mentioned by $g$ (its start symbol or one occurring in a production of $g$), $g$ has a production $B \to \alpha$ that is not a unit…

results.title: Productions of the unit-free grammar
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar, let $B$ be reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions of $g$, and let $B \to \beta$ be a production of $g$ whose right-hand side $\beta$ is not a single nonterminal. If $A$ is among the nonterminals mentioned by $g$, then $A \to \beta$ is a production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions.

results.title: Productions of the unit-eliminated grammar come from non-unit productions of $g$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For every production $A \to \beta$ of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions, there are a nonterminal $B$ and a production $B \to \beta$ of $g$ such that $\beta$ is not a single nonterminal and $B$ is reachable from $A$ by a possibly empty chain of unit productions of $g$.

results.title: Eliminating unit productions leaves no unit production
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, no production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions has an output consisting of a single nonterminal.

results.title: Eliminating unit productions creates no new outputs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. For every production of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions, some production of $g$ has the same output.

results.title: Languages along unit chains
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. If $B$ is reachable from $A$ by a chain of zero or more unit productions $A \to A_1 \to \dots \to B$ of $g$, then $L_g(B) \subseteq L_g(A)$.

results.title: Soundness of unit-production elimination
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and, for each nonterminal $A$, let $L_g(A)$ be the language of words $g$ derives from $A$. Then $L_g$ is a valuation of the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions: for every production $A \to \alpha$ of that grammar, the language of $\alpha$ under $L_g$ (the concatenation of the languages of its symbols, a terminal $a$ denoting $\{a\}$) is contained in $L_g(A)$.

results.title: Eliminating unit productions keeps every yield
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar. If a sentential form $\alpha$ of $g$ yields a terminal word $w$ in $g$, then $\alpha$ yields $w$ in the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions.

results.title: Eliminating unit productions preserves the language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the grammar obtained from $g$ by eliminating unit productions generates the same language as $g$.

results.title: Reduced grammars
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A context-free grammar is reduced when no production has empty right-hand side and no production has a single nonterminal as its right-hand side.

results.title: Existence of reduced grammars
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$ over an alphabet $T$ there is a context-free grammar $g'$ over $T$ that generates exactly the nonempty words generated by $g$, such that no production of $g'$ has empty right-hand side and no production of $g'$ has a single nonterminal as its right-hand side.

results.title: Variance components of the linear mixed model
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: The variance components of the linear mixed model `y = X β + g + e` with `g ~ N(0, σ_g² K)` and `e ~ N(0, σ_e² I)` on `n` individuals: a positive semidefinite genetic relationship matrix `K`, a genetic variance `σ_g² ≥ 0` and an environmental variance `σ_e² > 0`.

results.title: Marginal phenotypic covariance matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The marginal phenotypic covariance `V = σ_g² K + σ_e² I` of `y = X β + g + e`.

results.title: Positive definiteness of the phenotypic covariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `V = σ_g² K + σ_e² I` is positive definite.

results.title: Marginal log-likelihood of the mean
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The marginal log-likelihood of the mean `μ`: the log of the `N(μ, V)` density at `y`, `-(n log 2π + log det V + (y - μ)ᵀ V⁻¹ (y - μ)) / 2` (`det V > 0` by `posDef_V`).

results.title: Generalized least-squares estimator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generalized least-squares estimator `β̂ = (Xᵀ V⁻¹ X)⁻¹ Xᵀ V⁻¹ y`.

results.title: Residual-forming matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The residual-forming matrix `P = V⁻¹ - V⁻¹ X (Xᵀ V⁻¹ X)⁻¹ Xᵀ V⁻¹`.

results.title: GLS maximizes the marginal likelihood
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `X` of full column rank, every mean `X β` has marginal log-likelihood at most that of the GLS fit `X β̂`.

results.title: The GLS maximizer is unique
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `X` of full column rank, `X β` attains the maximal marginal log-likelihood only at `β = β̂`.

results.title: Maximal marginal log-likelihood
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The maximal marginal log-likelihood is `-(n log 2π + log det V + yᵀ P y) / 2`.

results.title: Residual-forming matrix annihilates the fixed effects
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `P X = 0`: the residual-forming matrix annihilates the fixed effects.

results.title: Identity $PVP = P$ for the residual-forming matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `P V P = P`. With `P X = 0`, this says that under the null model `y = X β + ε` with `Cov ε = V` the score `xᵀ P y = xᵀ P ε` has variance `xᵀ P V P x = xᵀ P x`.

results.title: Profile log-likelihood of a SNP effect
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The profile marginal log-likelihood of a SNP effect `γ` for the SNP genotype vector `x`: `sup_β logLik y (X β + γ x)`.

results.title: Score statistic for one SNP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The score statistic `(xᵀ P y)² / (xᵀ P x)` for one SNP `x`. Its denominator is positive when `x` is not in the column space of `X` (`info_pos`); otherwise the statistic is `0` by the convention `a / 0 = 0` and carries no information.

results.title: The profile log-likelihood of a SNP effect is an exact quadratic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `ℓ(γ) = ℓ(0) + γ xᵀ P y - γ² xᵀ P x / 2`, so its score at `γ = 0` is `xᵀ P y` and its information is `xᵀ P x`.

results.title: The score of a SNP effect
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The score of a SNP effect at `γ = 0` is `xᵀ P y`.

results.title: Score at the null generalized least-squares fit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The score is evaluated at the null GLS fit: `xᵀ P y = xᵀ V⁻¹ (y - X β̂)`.

results.title: Information of a SNP outside the column space of $X$ is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The information `xᵀ P x` is positive when the SNP `x` is not in the column space of `X`.

results.title: Best linear unbiased predictor of genetic effects
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The BLUP `ĝ = G V⁻¹ (y - X β̂)` of the genetic effects, with `G = σ_g² K` (Henderson 1975).

results.title: Solution of Henderson's mixed-model equations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: `(β, g)` solves Henderson's mixed-model equations with `R = σ_e² I` and `G = σ_g² K`, i.e. the specialization of `MixedModel.IsMMESolution` to `Z = 1` (every individual has its own genetic effect), `G = σ_g² K`, `R = σ_e² I`. In unfolded form this is `Xᵀ R⁻¹ X β + Xᵀ R⁻¹ g = Xᵀ R⁻¹ y` and `R⁻¹ X β + (R⁻¹ + G⁻¹) g = R⁻¹ y`. The equations are meaningful when `G` is invertible (`isMMESolution_iff`); otherwise `G⁻¹` is…

results.title: Henderson's mixed-model equations give the GLS estimator and the BLUP
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For positive definite `K`, `σ_g² > 0` and `X` of full column rank, `(β, g)` solves the mixed-model equations iff `β = β̂` and `g = σ_g² K V⁻¹ (y - X β̂)`. This is the specialization of `MixedModel.isMMESolution_iff_gls` to `Z = 1`, `G = σ_g² K`, `R = σ_e² I`; the generic theorem gives `β = glsMatrix X V *ᵥ y` and `g = G V⁻¹ (y - X β̂)`, which are `Model.gls` and `Model.blup` by the two conversion lemmas below.

results.title: Two-Gaussian mixture prior on a SNP effect
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The BOLT-LMM prior on a SNP effect: the mixture `p N(0, v₁) + (1 - p) N(0, v₂)` of two centered Gaussians with variances `v₁, v₂` (`v₂ = 0` gives the spike-and-slab prior with a point mass at `0`).

results.title: Mixture prior is a probability measure
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mixture prior is a probability measure for a mixing weight `p ≤ 1`.

results.title: Mixture prior has finite second moment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mixture prior has a finite second moment.

results.title: Admissible variational factor
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: An admissible variational factor for the prior `π`: a probability measure with a finite second moment and finite KL divergence from `π` (`q ≪ π` with integrable log-likelihood ratio).

results.title: Mean of a variational factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean `∫ b dq` of a factor.

results.title: Squared norm of a genotype column
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The squared norm `‖xⱼ‖² = ∑ᵢ X i j ²` of the genotype column of SNP `j`.

results.title: Expected residual sum of squares under the variational factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected residual sum of squares `‖y - X μ‖² + ∑ⱼ ‖xⱼ‖² vⱼ` of the product of the factors `q`, with means `μⱼ` and variances `vⱼ` (`integral_rss_pi`).

results.title: The expected residual sum of squares of a product of factors
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For probability factors with finite second moments, `𝔼_{∏ qⱼ} ‖y - X β‖² = ‖y - X μ‖² + ∑ⱼ ‖xⱼ‖² vⱼ`.

results.title: Mean-field evidence lower bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The mean-field evidence lower bound `-(n/2) log (2π σ_e²) - 𝔼_q ‖y - X β‖² / (2 σ_e²) - ∑ⱼ KL(qⱼ ‖ π)`, meaningful for `σ_e² > 0`. It is the ELBO for admissible factors (finite KL); for an inadmissible factor `toReal` would turn an infinite divergence into `0`, so all results assume admissibility.

results.title: Partial residual of a SNP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The partial residual `rⱼ = y - ∑_{k ≠ j} xₖ μₖ` of the other SNPs' posterior means.

results.title: Coordinate-ascent potential for one SNP effect
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The CAVI potential `fⱼ(b) = (b xⱼᵀ rⱼ - ‖xⱼ‖² b² / 2) / σ_e²`: the part of the expected log-likelihood `𝔼_{q_{-j}}[log p(y | β)]` that depends on `βⱼ = b` (`exists_elbo_update_eq`).

results.title: Coordinate-ascent update of one variational factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The CAVI update of factor `j`: the prior tilted by the potential, `qⱼ ∝ π · exp fⱼ = exp 𝔼_{q_{-j}}[log p(y, β)]`.

results.title: One coordinate-ascent step
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: One coordinate-ascent step: replace factor `j` by its CAVI update.

results.title: Coordinate ascent along an update schedule
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Coordinate ascent along the update schedule `s`: at time `t` factor `s t` is updated.

results.title: The ELBO as a function of one factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With the other factors fixed, the ELBO of `q` with factor `j` replaced by an admissible `q'` is `∫ fⱼ dq' - KL(q' ‖ π) + C`.

results.title: Coordinate-ascent update is an admissible factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The CAVI update is an admissible factor, for a probability prior with a finite second moment.

results.title: The CAVI update maximizes the ELBO over its factor, with exact gap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Replacing factor `j` by an admissible `q'` gives `ELBO(caviStep q j) - KL(q' ‖ caviUpdate q j)`.

results.title: Coordinate ascent does not decrease the ELBO
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Coordinate ascent does not decrease the ELBO.

results.title: The ELBO is nondecreasing along coordinate ascent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ELBO is nondecreasing along coordinate ascent, for any update schedule.

results.title: Stationary points of coordinate ascent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No admissible change of factor `j` increases the ELBO iff `qⱼ` is the expected-log-joint update `π · exp fⱼ / Z`.
